title: fea.runOptions
summary: Create family-specific typed FEA run options.
description: `fea.runOptions(solver, Name, Value, ...)` creates a `fea.RunOptions` object whose schema is selected by the solver family.
behaviors: Count and iteration fields are nonnegative exact structural scalars at construction. All eight integer classes and ordinary integral doubles are accepted exactly; fractional, nonfinite, negative, out-of-range, nonscalar, and resident controls reject. Solver-specific positivity checks run before execution.

Tolerance, time, scale, ratio, exponent, frequency, and residual fields are real physical scalars. Integer inputs cross once into binary64 after kind, field, and scalar-shape validation; solver-specific finiteness and range checks run before execution.
Logical controls require logical scalars. `PrecisionMode`, `PreconditionerMode`, and `QualityPolicy` are text.
Unknown or duplicate normalized options reject before object construction. Structural option properties remain exact typed integers; true floating options remain double.
integer_forms: Exact electromagnetic: `HarmonicMaxIterations` 96. Floating electromagnetic: `ResidualTarget` 1e-6, `HarmonicTolerance` 1e-7, and finite `SweepFrequencyHz` values.
defaults: Every family defaults `DeterministicMode` to false, `PrecisionMode` to `fp64`, and `QualityPolicy` to `balanced`.
`linear_static` additionally defaults `PreconditionerMode` to `auto` and has no numeric count or physical scalar option.
Transient defaults `AdaptiveTimeStep` to true; nonlinear defaults `LineSearch` to true; electromagnetic defaults `SweepEnabled` to false and `SweepFrequencyHz` to empty.

examples.description: Configure an exact transient step count

faqs.question: Why is an integer accepted for a tolerance?
faqs.answer: It is accepted as a finite real scalar and converted once to the option's binary64 physics field; count fields instead remain exact integers.
